## Page 1 | H9-A: draft note for the director

**To:** Director, programme investment<br>
**Subject:** GreenWaste national expansion<br>
**Status:** Draft for review; fictional training case

Read the recommendation and Table T9. This note is separate from the Day 4 report.

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d9_note_html())
```

### T9 | Annual waste-cost saving at 12 months

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d9_results_table())
```

**Unit:** AED per business per year; positive = lower waste cost. Each row has a 95% interval on that saving scale. The policy rule is a **minimum annual saving of 1,000 AED**.

The pilot is a separate district sample. The three city methods reuse the same city records. The economic ratio in N3 is a partial RCT-linked model; its cost and later savings are assumed.

<p class="caption">Paragraph IDs N1–N3; table ID T9. These results concern different comparisons, not four independent estimates of one national effect.</p>

</div>

<div class="sheet-page" id="H9-B">

## Page 2 | H9-B: comparison and question map

An estimate becomes useful when its **comparison, population, assumption and uncertainty** fit the decision.

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d9_table(d9_map))
```

### Five places to look for a decision gap

1. **Comparison and reach:** who was compared, and does that population match national delivery?
2. **Causal requirement:** what would challenge the lottery, trend, cut-off or matching interpretation?
3. **Uncertainty and rule:** does the interval support the minimum-saving claim?
4. **Data quality:** who was followed up, and how were outcomes measured?
5. **Economic inputs:** what was spent, when, by whom, and how long might savings last?

<p class="caption">The city file has 10,000 businesses, including 4,794 participants. The separate pilot has 400 businesses in one district. This map identifies questions; it does not certify that the requirements hold.</p>

</div>

<div class="sheet-page">

## Page 5 | Advice to the director

Work alone. Compare your answer with your opening decision on page 3.

**1. Action:** sign, sign with conditions, or request evidence.
<div class="writing tall"></div>

**2. Basis:** cite one source and say precisely what it establishes.
<div class="writing tall"></div>

**3. Boundary:** what does that source not establish for national expansion?
<div class="writing tall"></div>

**4. Next step:** name one document/result and explain what you would do if it supports or challenges the claim.
<div class="writing tall"></div>

**My decision changed / stayed the same because:**
<div class="writing tall"></div>

<p class="caption">A conditional next phase or a request for evidence can both be defensible. The quality of the reasoning matters more than which option was selected.</p>

</div>
